title: The Tao that can be told
word: The Tao that can be told
hookLine: the Tao that can be spoken is not the eternal Tao; the nameless is the origin (Tao Te Ching 1)
carry: not the one that can be told

lines: THE WORDS POINT. THEY DON'T ARRIVE.
A BOOK THAT BEGINS WITH A WARNING.
cards: How would you describe the taste of water to someone who had never had any? Cool, maybe. Wet.
Plain. Every word slides off it. Or the smell of rain on a hot sidewalk, or the face of someone you love: you can talk for an hour and still not hand it over.
The words point; they don't arrive. The Tao Te Ching opens with a warning like that: what it's about can't be fully told, and the moment you've said it, you've already missed it a little.

teach.b: First, the opening line, in James Legge's translation: "The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name."
In Chinese the line opens with one character used twice, first as a noun and then as a verb: the Tao that can be Tao'd. That character can mean a road, and it can also mean to say.
Legge chose the road, a way you can walk; other translators choose the speaking, a way you can tell. The line makes sense either way: any Tao you can map or describe is not the whole of it.
Second, the nameless and the named. Thought of as having no name, the chapter says, the Tao is the origin of heaven and earth; thought of as having a name, it is the mother of all things.
The nameless is where everything comes from. The named is where people live: kitchens, cities, words for every tree. Third, both are the same.
The two come from one source and only get different names as things unfold. The chapter doesn't ask you to throw words away; every name is a small door into something larger than the name.
Fourth, the mystery has a gate.

teach.h: NOT THE ONE THAT CAN BE TOLD.
teach.b: The chapter ends by calling the deepest point of this mystery a gate, the way in to all that is subtle and wonderful. The book written at a gate opens with one.

how: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching return to its opening chapter again and again, and some Taoist teachers treat it as a reminder that every description of the Way falls short of the Way itself.

games.q: what does “the tao that can be told” mean?
o: the opening line: a Tao you can tell isn't the lasting one
a saying that only spoken teachings can be trusted
a promise that the book will explain the Tao fully

games.q: inside chapter one: tap the pairs.
p: the origin of heaven and earth
Legge's word: a road you walk
the way in to the mystery

s: the Tao Te Ching opens by defining the Tao clearly
it opens by warning that the Tao that can be trodden, or told, is not the enduring Tao.
the same Chinese character in the first line can mean a road and to say
Legge chose the road, trodden; other translators choose the speaking.
chapter one tells readers to give up words
it says the nameless and the named come from one source; every name is a small door into something larger.

games.q: someone asks the old master to explain the Tao in one clear sentence. what does chapter one do?
o: say that the Tao that can be told is not the enduring Tao.
refuse to say anything at all.
games.why: it speaks, and in the same breath warns that what it speaks of is more than the words. then it keeps going for the rest of the book.

practice: Look at something ordinary, a cup, a leaf, your own hand, and name it once, quietly. Then keep looking past the name, at the color where the light hits it and the small shadow underneath, letting each new word go.
If you pray, you can rest in what can't be named; if not, just stay with what's still there after the words run out.

wordCard.voice: The Tao that can be told. The opening line of the Tao Te Ching, which says that any way you can tread or tell is not the enduring Tao. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese, wú míng: no name, nameless. Chapter one says the nameless is the origin of heaven and earth.

carryVoice: Your line: not the one that can be told. A person, a mood, a day: each is more than its name. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
